title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
NonStationaryBrachistochrone provides symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure generators and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. It supports the companion studies of FLRW and Vaidya geometries (Paper I) and conformal Kerr, or Thakurta–Kerr, spacetimes (Paper II).

This release improves the accessibility and reliability of the reproduction workflow.

  • English reproduction chain. Comments, docstrings and printed messages in the main reproduction scripts are now in English. Program headers describe their assumptions, outputs and limitations. Historical working notes remain in Italian and are identified as such.
  • Repaired Mathematica checks. The Thakurta–Kerr t-branch checks now use the correct energy derivative, preserve the drift-clock normalisation and compare against identifiable Python references obtained through ODE integration and quadrature. These benchmarks check response integrals contributing to the first-order correction, rather than the complete non-autonomous dynamics.
  • Reproducible figures. Diagnostic plots no longer overwrite manuscript figures. The Paper I off-shell validation figure and its attribution have been corrected.
  • Reliable build failures. The Paper I build returns a non-zero status when generation, collection, required figures or LaTeX compilation fail. Ten standalone regression tests cover successful and failing build scenarios.
  • Consistent filenames. The `_codex` suffix has been removed from 16 filenames, with imports, commands and documentation updated accordingly.

Verification included a clean GitHub checkout with a fresh Python environment installed from requirements-lock.txt: 12 regression checks, six Sage checks, parser tests, the repaired Mathematica comparisons and provenance verification passed. The corrected Paper I build regenerated all 13 required figures and produced a 67-page manuscript.

Generated figures, compiled PDFs and raw datasets are regenerated using the documented commands. Verification maps distinguish symbolic identities, numerical checks, sampled evidence and archived certificates.
